1.title: SmartMaid — Home Services
1.desc: Book verified cleaning workers and companies in a minute — Escrow payments, voice search and GPS booking.
1.problem: Hiring domestic help stays informal: no verification, no secure payment, and no accountability when something goes wrong.
1.solution: KYC-verified workers and companies, money held in Escrow until the job is done, Arabic voice search, GPS booking, and an admin panel with 59 control switches.
1.result: Book in a minute with price and rating up front — money only moves when both sides are satisfied.

2.title: Mukallaf — Iraqi Tax System
2.desc: Full Arabic tax platform for Iraqi companies, accountants and taxpayers — seven tax modules in one place.
2.problem: Tax work in Iraq was done by hand: wrong brackets, missed deadlines and avoidable fines.
2.solution: Seven modules (payroll, annual settlement, corporate, contracts, real estate, land, free professions) with brackets per Income Tax Law 113/1982, official form generation, deadlines, penalties, roles and Excel/PDF export.
2.result: One Arabic platform where every return is calculated, generated and tracked — from data entry to a printable official form.

3.title: Flossk — Iraqi Money Assistant
3.desc: First Iraqi budget app with a voice assistant that understands your dialect — free, offline, no ads.
3.problem: Iraqi users manage money with paper or foreign apps that ignore the dinar, local habits and the Arabic language.
3.solution: Income, expenses and deductions with an 80+ command voice assistant, multi-wallet, debts, 11 currencies with IQD default and reports — all stored locally, working offline.
3.result: A 100% Arabic, offline-first money app: data stays on the device, everything runs by voice, free forever.

4.title: Bookly — Bookings & Stays
4.desc: Arabic booking platform for farms, chalets, hotels, apartments, flights, cars and tours with instant refunds.
4.problem: Booking farms and chalets in Iraq runs on phone calls and DMs — no clear prices, no refunds, no trust.
4.solution: A four-step booking flow, a digital wallet with instant refunds, loyalty points, and a supplier dashboard for calendars, prices and payouts.
4.result: Guests book and pay with a clear summary and get refunds to the wallet instantly; suppliers run everything from one dashboard.

5.title: Ziona Passports — Servers & CCTV
5.desc: IT operations for a passport office: servers, printers, cameras and the link to the central system.
5.problem: Passport-printing systems and cameras kept failing, blocking daily operations.
5.solution: Ran and maintained office servers, printers and camera systems, and wired the link to the central passports server.
5.result: Stable day-to-day operations with faster fault recovery across the office.

6.title: Hala Sat — Fiber Internet Support
6.desc: Field diagnostics and customer support for fiber subscribers across Baghdad.
6.problem: Subscribers across Baghdad hit outages and slow lines with no fast local response.
6.solution: Diagnosed fiber lines on site, resolved customer and infrastructure faults, and documented fixes for the team.
6.result: Quicker restoration times and a repeatable process for common fiber faults.

about.label: 03 / About
about.text: I'm Hussein — an IT manager and software engineer from Baghdad who has built an ERP from scratch, kept servers alive and shipped apps.
about.body1: I graduated from the University of Diyala and started in the field: passport-printing servers, CCTV and IT for real offices — then fiber support for hundreds of subscribers.
about.body2: Today I lead IT at a Baghdad company where I built a custom ERP that replaced Odoo entirely — and I still ship full stack web and Flutter apps, design and social, because one person can carry all of it.
about.p1p: Servers, fiber, CCTV and networking — fixed under real production pressure, not in a lab.
about.p2p: Infrastructure, backend, web, mobile app and design — no hand-offs, no coordination tax.
about.p3p: Years managing sales and social media for shops and clinics — I know what the software has to earn.

experience.e1d: Designed and built a custom ERP from scratch that fully replaced commercial suites like Odoo, led all IT infrastructure — servers, systems and internal networks — and delivered 10+ software projects and websites.
experience.e2d: Kept passport printing systems, servers and cameras running, and maintained the server connectivity with government systems.
experience.e3d: Diagnosed and resolved fiber optic connectivity and service issues for subscribers across Baghdad.
experience.e4r: Remote Sales Manager & Social Media Administrator
experience.e4d: Managed sales operations and social media accounts, and led digital marketing campaigns that grew engagement and brand reach.
experience.e5d: Full stack web and Flutter mobile apps for iOS and Android — custom software shaped around each business's real workflow.

testimonials.label: 06 / Voices
testimonials.q1: Hussein took over our servers, printers and cameras when nothing else was stable — faults that used to stop the office all day now get fixed the same morning.
testimonials.q2: Our fiber subscribers used to wait days for a response. He answered on site, fixed the line and wrote down the fix so the whole team could repeat it.

faq.label: 07 / FAQ
faq.a1: Full stack websites and dashboards, Flutter apps for iOS and Android, network and server infrastructure, and the brand design around them — usually all four for the same client.
faq.q2: Do you work in Arabic and English?
faq.a2: Yes. Every product I ship is designed in both — Arabic with full right-to-left support, English for international audiences.
faq.a3: Send a message or book a call. We talk about the problem, I send scope, price and timeline, and work starts once you approve. No surprise costs.
faq.q4: How long does a project take?
faq.a4: A business site: 1–2 weeks. A full platform or app: 4–10 weeks depending on modules. Infrastructure and support work is scheduled around your hours.
faq.q5: Do you maintain what you build?
faq.a5: Yes — updates, monitoring, backups and fixes after launch, as a monthly retainer or per request.
faq.a6: Baghdad, Iraq (UTC+3). I work remotely with clients anywhere and handle on-site work across Baghdad.
faq.q7: Does this site use cookies or analytics?
faq.a7: No cookie is set here and no analytics vendor is in the path. The counter keeps one salted hash of an ip address per Baghdad day, so the same visit cannot count twice, and nothing that names anybody — the privacy page lists every piece of it.
faq.q8: Which languages can a product ship in?
faq.a8: Arabic and English as standard, both with the full layout in their own direction. This site itself is written in twelve languages from one translation file, so adding yours to a product is an edit, not a rebuild.
faq.q9: What do you need from me to begin?
faq.a9: What exists and what hurts: the pages, screens or systems involved, any logo and text you already have, and who approves the work. That is enough for a written scope, price and dates — and the work starts when you say so.
faq.q10: Do I see the work while it is still being built?
faq.a10: Yes: a preview link every week rather than a reveal at the end. Every stage is one message away, and the answers are on this sheet before you have to ask.

pricing.label: 08 / Pricing
pricing.note: Every project gets a fixed written quote before work starts — no hourly surprises. These are honest starting points; the final price depends on scope.
pricing.p1d: 5–7 pages, Arabic + English, contact form, fast hosting, delivered in ~2 weeks.
pricing.p2d: Accounts, payments, admin dashboards, full RTL — built like Mukallaf or Bookly.
pricing.p3d: iOS + Android from one codebase, clean UI, store submission included.
pricing.p4d: Windows/Linux servers, office network, CCTV — installed, secured and documented.
pricing.p5d: Monthly content plan, designs, posting and Meta ads management for your pages.
pricing.p6d: Logo, color system and ready-to-use templates for print and social.
pricing.p7d: Domain purchase, DNS, business email addresses and first-year hosting setup.
pricing.p8d: Custom software and ERP modules — scoped and quoted after a short call.
pricing.custom: Need something else? Any electronic service — ask for it.

proc.label: SPEC / Process
proc.p1: You describe the problem in your own words. I repeat it back, add what you left out, and we agree the target before anything is priced.
proc.p2: A written scope: pages or screens, features, what is excluded, one fixed price and real dates. The number in this document is the number on the invoice.
proc.p3: Work happens in the open — a preview link you can click every week, built from the Arabic layout first rather than translated from English afterwards.
proc.p4: Deployed, tested on real devices, handed over with the accounts, keys and a short written guide. You own the repository, the domain, the hosting.
proc.p5: The same desk that answered during the build answers after it — server faults, printer queues, camera records and the next feature.
proc.note: Every stage is one message away — ask at any point and you get the answer the sheet already shows.

p.lead: This site counts its own visitors. No analytics vendor, no advertising cookie, no third-party font request — what a page learns about a visit, this page tells you.
p.countP: Once per day, Baghdad time: a salted hash of your ip address, the page that sent you here, and the device family your browser reports. The salt changes, so the same person cannot be followed from one day to the next.
p.never1: No cookie is set by this site.
p.never2: No advertising id, pixel or cross-site tracker.
p.never3: No full ip address is stored, and nothing that names you.
p.never4: No name, email or phone number unless you send the order form.
p.formP: The order form carries your name, email, phone, the service, budget, deadline and message to this site’s own database and to the mailbox that answers you. It is used to reply and to prepare an estimate — not for marketing, not sold, not passed to anybody else.
p.hostP: Hosting, database, mail and the captcha each belong to one provider, and each receives only what its part needs. The captcha script is fetched only when a form reaches the step that asks for it, and not at all when that step is off.
p.askP: Write to the contact address on the homepage. If you sent a request, ask and you can see it, correct it, or have it deleted; a plain question gets a plain answer, not a form.

t.lead: Using this site means agreeing to the rules below. They are short on purpose: written for the person reading them, not for a lawyer filing them.
t.workP: The projects and case studies describe real work for real clients, with figures as they were measured or agreed at the time. Screenshots and artwork belong to the products they show, and nothing here is a promise about your project.
t.priceP: The estimator and any number in a reply are an indication in US dollars, valid for the period stated in that message. A price binds only in a written agreement between both sides.
t.reqP: Please give a correct email — a request with a wrong address cannot be answered. One request per project; the form is rate-limited and captcha-protected, so bulk or automated submissions are refused. Nothing sent creates an obligation until an agreement is signed.
t.useP: You may read, link to and print these pages while you decide about the work. You may not scrape the site in bulk, replay its forms, probe its infrastructure, or present its text, artwork or case studies as your own.
t.yoursP: What you send in a message remains yours. It carries no licence beyond what is needed to answer you, and your name or company appears only where you have agreed it.
t.outP: GitHub, WhatsApp, mail and a few product pages lead off this site. Their behaviour and policies belong to them; the link is a courtesy, not an endorsement or a guarantee.
t.lawP: These terms, and any work agreed after them, follow the law of the Republic of Iraq with Baghdad as the place of performance. Neither side answers for indirect or incidental loss, and responsibility for a project never exceeds what that project paid.
